issue.title: Bug: protocol detection for custom provider shows 'Post .../systemone: EOF' while endpoint responds 200 OK to curl
issue.body:
## Summary

When adding a custom provider whose Base URL protocol tab is set to **System One** and clicking "Detect protocol" (检测协议), the UI shows:

```
× Post "https://<host>/v1/systemone": EOF
```

even though the endpoint responds successfully to a direct request.

## Environment

- magpie version: 0.1.1560
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu), proxy in use (HTTPS_PROXY=http://192.168.0.111:7890)
- Provider type: custom, protocol tab "System One"
- Base URL: https://api.subq.ai/v1
- Model: subq-snap-1.1

## Reproduction

1. Open "Custom provider" (自定义供应商) dialog.
2. Name: SubQ, Base URL: https://api.subq.ai/v1
3. Select the "System One" protocol tab.
4. Enter API key and model `subq-snap-1.1`.
5. Click "Detect protocol" (检测协议).

Result: red error `× Post "https://api.subq.ai/v1/systemone": EOF`.

## Expected

Detection should succeed because the endpoint is reachable and returns a valid response.

## Verification that the endpoint works

Direct request (no magpie involved) returns HTTP 200 with a valid JSON body:

```
$ curl -sS -X POST https://api.subq.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"subq-snap-1.1","state":"...","questions":{"escalate":{"type":"noul","instructions":"...","criteria":{"true":"...","false":"..."}}}}'
{"model":"subq-snap-1.1","answers":{"escalate":{"type":"noul","noul":0.9758...}},"usage":{"input_tokens":128,"output_tokens":0}}
```

Also verified:
- HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 both return 200.
- Without proxy, returns 200.
- Various User-Agent strings (including `Go-http-client/1.1`) return 200.
- Python `http.client` HTTPSConnection returns 200.
- Invalid/empty bodies return HTTP 422 validation errors, not EOF.

So the server never closes the connection prematurely; the EOF happens inside magpie's HTTP client during the detection request.

## Notes

- `magpie provider test <id>` for the same provider's `decide` entry returns "SubQ lists no models", which may be related.
- API key redacted; available on request.

comments.body:
`Detect protocol` posts System One's question through `http.DefaultClient`, and magpie's own requests never carried Go's replay mark: a POST written into a keep-alive connection that a proxy or the vendor's front had already dropped was read as `EOF` and failed, while the same POST on a fresh connection got 200 (which is why curl, opening one, worked). Your setup has a proxy in play, the case where those idle connections get dropped.

The gateway's upstream POSTs have carried the mark (`X-Idempotency-Key`, read by Go's transport and never written on the wire) since #2136; the editor's Test, Detect APIs, System One detection and model lists did not.

This branch moves that mark into `netproxy.Dispatch`, which `netproxy.Install` (magpie's own client) and the gateway's transports both go through, so a detection whose connection was dropped is sent again at once on a new one, and the gateway's behaviour is unchanged.

[fix/3665-bug-protocol-detection-for-custom](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3665-bug-protocol-detection-for-custom), commit f476cbc8283ebf48c2d11214da5dfe7d796bf9c3

Run: `TestSystemOneDetectionOutlivesADroppedKeepAlive` (fails before the change with `SubQ: Post …/v1/systemone: EOF`, passes after, also `-count=5`), `go test ./internal/netproxy/`, `go test ./internal/gateway/ -run TestDroppedKeepAliveIsAskedAgainAtOnce` (the #2136 guarantee still holds), `go test ./internal/gui/ -run Detect`, `go build ./...`, cross-OS builds and `go vet` on the three packages. `go test ./internal/provider/` has 4 failures that also fail with this change reverted to upstream/main on this host (three multiprotocol model-list counts and TestCodexAppServersOnHome). The full `internal/gateway` suite was not completed — the machine was running four lanes' copies of it at once — so it is the one check left unrun.

This is a fork branch, ready to review — not a claim on the issue's ownership.
